newsitem.title: CANADA: Bell Canada forecasts higher 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Bell Canada forecasts higher 1997 earnings.

text.p: Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc said on Wednesday it hopes to make bigger profits in 1997.
Net income is forecast to rise to C$850 million in 1997 from C$714 million in 1996, Bell said in a statement outlining its financial targets for the year.
The telephone company also targeted a return on equity of 11.7 percent in 1997, up from 9.8 percent.
Bell said it anticipated operating cash flow to climb to C$3 billion this year from C$2.8 billion in 1996.
"Although these represent very good results, there is still room for growth in providing a fair return to shareholders," said chief executive John McLennan.
He said the numbers fall short of preliminary targets set in March 1995 which formed the basis for a filing with Canadian regulators in mid-1996.
McLennan said the company was on course to meet its March 1995 target of cutting more than 10,000 jobs by the end of 1997.
The targets reflect the company's need to grow and become more globally competitive, he said.
